question: Why do persons arise when the supreme Lord is already full even in personhood?
premises: The supreme Lord remains full even when personhood is attained.
In that state there is non-recognition of his own nature.
This non-recognition is described as wondrous and gives rise to persons.
inference: Personhood arises through non-recognition of the Lord's own full nature, not through any lack in the Lord.
plain_english: Thus, even when the supreme Lord, though full, has attained personhood, there is non-recognition of his own nature. This is wondrous indeed, and from it persons arise.
